candidate_relations.label: Oral ulcerative lesions, tongue
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record confirms an ulcerative lesion on the tongue, so this descriptor is anatomically compatible, but it is a purely descriptive/morphological term lacking the required etiologic specificity (Histoplasma capsulatum infection) and the 'primary oral' qualifier that distinguishes this from secondary oral histoplasmosis in disseminated disease
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Describes the anatomical site and morphological presentation (ulcer on tongue) but does not specify the etiologic diagnosis of histoplasmosis or its primary/isolated oral nature

case_quality_flags: Negative fungal culture despite positive histopathology is noted; culture negativity does not exclude histoplasmosis and is acknowledged in the record
Geographic context (eastern India) and immunocompetent host with isolated oral lesion support primary oral histoplasmosis as the reference diagnosis
